questions.stem: The degree of the polynomial \(P(x) = 6x^4-4x^3+3x^5-x+1\) is:
questions.hint: The degree is the highest power of \(x\) appearing — rewrite the terms in descending order first.

steps.explain: Rewrite the terms in descending order of power.
The degree is the highest power present.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows the graph of a cubic function with leading coefficient of −3?
questions.hint: A cubic with a negative leading coefficient rises on the left and falls on the right. It has opposite end behaviour.

steps.explain: A cubic has odd degree, so its two ends point in opposite directions.
steps.work: For large |x|, the leading term −3x³ controls the graph.

steps.explain: Because the leading coefficient is negative, the left end rises and the right end falls.
Only diagram B has this end behaviour and a cubic shape.

keyPoints.note: Use the end behaviour determined by the leading term −3x³.

questions.hint: Expand the left side, then compare the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant terms with the right side.

steps.explain: Expand the left side: multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second.
Compare the constant terms (no \(x\)): \(-2k=10\).
Compare the coefficients of \(x\): \(k-2=a\). Substitute \(k=-5\).
Check by expanding with \(k=-5\): \((x-2)(x-5)=x^{2}-7x+10\) ✓ (\(a=-7\), constant 10).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Expand, then match the constant terms and the x terms.

topics.title: The remainder theorem and factor theorem

questions.stem: The remainder when \(3x^3-7x^2+2x+4\) is divided by \((x-3)\) is:
questions.hint: By the remainder theorem, the remainder equals \(P(3)\).

steps.explain: By the remainder theorem, substitute \(x=3\) into the polynomial.
Evaluate.

questions.stem: (b) When the polynomial \(P(x)=x^3-ax^2+x\) is divided by \((x-3)\), the remainder is 12. Find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x+1)\).
questions.hint: Use the remainder theorem: substitute \(x=3\) to find \(a\), then substitute \(x=-1\) into \(P(x)\) to find the required remainder.

steps.explain: By the remainder theorem, \(P(3)=12\). Substitute and solve for \(a\).
Solve for \(a\).
Now find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x+1)\), which by the remainder theorem is \(P(-1)\).
Evaluate.

questions.hint: Factor out 3, test x=1, and factor the remaining quadratic.

steps.explain: Remove the common factor 3.
Test x=1 and divide by (x−1).
Factor and solve.

keyPoints.note: Take out 3, find a simple root, then factor the remaining quadratic.

questions.stem: If \(P(x)=3x^3-7x^2+2x+4\), divide \(P(x)\) by \(x-3\). Give your answer in the form \(P(x)=Q(x)(x-3)+R(x)\).
questions.hint: Set the divisor \(x-3\) equal to zero to find the synthetic value. Bring down the first coefficient, then multiply by \(3\) and add at each column. The last result is the remainder.

steps.explain: For synthetic division, first find the value that makes the divisor zero. Then write the coefficients of the dividend in descending powers of \(x\), including a coefficient for every power.
Bring down the leading coefficient \(3\). Multiply it by the synthetic value \(3\), then add that product to the next coefficient \(-7\).
Use the new bottom value \(2\). Multiply it by \(3\), then add the product to the next original coefficient \(2\).
Multiply the latest bottom value \(8\) by \(3\), then add the product to the final original coefficient \(4\). The final bottom value is the remainder.
The bottom row before the final number gives the quotient coefficients, in descending powers. The final number is the remainder.
Check by multiplying out the quotient times the divisor and then adding the remainder. The result must match the original polynomial.

keyPoints.note: Use synthetic value \(3\) because \(x-3=0\) when \(x=3\). The final synthetic-division result is the remainder.

questions.stem: Given \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2\) and \(Q(x)=x+2\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(Q(x)\)?
questions.hint: Remainder theorem: the remainder on dividing by \(x-a\) is \(P(a)\). Here \(x+2=x-(-2)\), so find \(P(-2)\).

steps.explain: Write \(x+2\) as \(x-(-2)\): \(a=-2\). The remainder is \(P(-2)\).
Substitute \(x=-2\) (careful with the signs of the powers: \((-2)^{3}=-8\), \((-2)^{2}=4\)).
Add.
The remainder is 0, so \((x+2)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) (factor theorem), which we use in the next part.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Remainder theorem: substitute the root of the divisor.

questions.stem: Given \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2\), which has the factor \(x+2\). Express \(P(x)\) as a product of its factors.
questions.hint: Divide \(P(x)\) by \((x+2)\) (long division) to get the quadratic quotient, then factorise it completely.

steps.explain: Factorise the quadratic \(2x^{2}-3x+1\): numbers with product \(2\times1=2\) and sum \(-3\) are \(-2\) and \(-1\): \(2x^{2}-2x-x+1=2x(x-1)-(x-1)\).
Full factorisation (option D is NOT complete, it still contains a factorisable quadratic).
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.text: Express \(P(x)\) as a product of its factors
keyPoints.note: Divide by the known factor, then factorise the quotient completely.

questions.stem: Hence or otherwise sketch \(y=P(x)\) showing \(x\) and \(y\)-intercepts, where \(P(x)=2x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+2=(x+2)(2x-1)(x-1)\). Which sketch (A, B, C or D in the figure) is correct?
questions.hint: \(x\)-intercepts from the factors; \(y\)-intercept \(=P(0)\) (the constant term); the leading term \(2x^{3}\) is positive, so the graph goes from bottom-left to top-right.

steps.explain: \(x\)-intercepts: set each factor to 0: \(x+2=0\), \(2x-1=0\), \(x-1=0\). Three single roots, so the curve crosses the axis at each (green).
\(y\)-intercept: \(P(0)=2\) (the constant term), the orange point \((0,2)\).
End behaviour: the \(x^{3}\) coefficient is \(+2>0\), so \(y\to+\infty\) as \(x\to\infty\) and \(y\to-\infty\) as \(x\to-\infty\) (bottom-left to top-right).

Shape: coming up from the bottom-left it crosses at \(-2\), rises to a local maximum, comes down through \((0,2)\)... then crosses \(x=\dfrac{1}{2}\), dips to a local minimum and crosses at \(x=1\) going up.
steps.work: \(\text{cross at }-2,\ \dfrac{1}{2},\ 1\ \text{with a max then a min}\)

steps.explain: Compare options: B is upside-down (negative leading coefficient); C has roots at \(2,-\dfrac{1}{2},-1\) (signs wrong); D is shifted down (\(y\)-intercept \(-2\)). Only A matches.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Roots from the factors, y-intercept from the constant term, ends from the sign of the x cubed term.
